findings.title: Resource leak: opened files are never closed
findings.body: The new code opens a file on line 7 and appends the handle to `_open_reports` on line 8, but never closes any of the collected file objects. This leaks file descriptors and can exhaust system resources. Close each file after reading or use a context manager.
findings.suggestion:
with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as report:
        return report.read()

findings.title: Global list of file handles breaks encapsulation
findings.body: The new global `_open_reports` list exposes internal resources to callers and invites misuse. It also couples the module’s state to its callers, making the function non-reentrant and harder to test. Remove the list and close the file immediately after reading.

findings.title: Violates Clean Architecture: resource management in application code
findings.body: Opening and managing file handles belongs in infrastructure, not in the application layer. Application code should delegate I/O to ports/adapters. Move file handling to an infrastructure module and keep `read_report` as a pure function.

summary.problem: The change leaks file descriptors and mixes resource management with application logic.
summary.done_well: The function signature and return type remain clean and focused.
